boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Vallejo destinations on the downtown waterfront and Mare Island corridors, each with a documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Vallejo Ferry Terminal
cards.subtitle: Mare Island Way and Georgia Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk the terminal edge to orient yourself to Vallejo’s waterfront; the city identifies this as the year-round Bay Ferry connection to San Francisco.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront transit landmark with a direct San Francisco connection.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Vallejo states that year-round San Francisco Bay Ferry service operates from the Vallejo Ferry Terminal at Mare Island Way and Georgia Street.
cards.access_notes: Ferry travel requires checking the operator’s current schedule and fares.

cards.title: Empress Theatre
cards.subtitle: Virginia Street corridor
cards.notes: Pause beneath the historic marquee, then use the theatre’s calendar to choose an all-ages-appropriate performance or film before buying tickets.
cards.short_summary: A 1911 downtown theatre with a prominent street-facing marquee.
cards.evidence_claim: The Empress Theatre identifies its Vallejo location as 330 Virginia Street and states that it was established in 1911.
cards.access_notes: Box-office and event access vary; confirm the specific event before visiting.

cards.title: Vallejo John F. Kennedy Library
cards.subtitle: Santa Clara Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the library’s group study rooms or visit the first-floor McCune Collection, which includes rare books on California and book arts.
cards.short_summary: A public-library stop combining study space with local special collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Solano County Library lists the Vallejo John F. Kennedy Library at 505 Santa Clara Street, with group study rooms and the McCune Collection on its first floor.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours; study rooms are first-come, first-served when available.

cards.title: Vallejo Naval & Historical Museum
cards.subtitle: Marin Street corridor
cards.notes: Plan for the five galleries and the working submarine periscope, then confirm operating hours before heading to historic Old City Hall.
cards.short_summary: A local-history museum connecting Vallejo and Mare Island’s naval past.
cards.evidence_claim: The Vallejo Naval & Historical Museum says it is housed in historic Old City Hall at 734 Marin Street and has five galleries plus a working submarine periscope.
cards.source_title: About Us | Vallejo Naval & Historical Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Tuesday–Friday and Saturday visitor hours; verify before arrival.

cards.title: Artiszen Cultural Arts Center
cards.subtitle: Georgia Street corridor
cards.notes: Look for current exhibitions, workshops, or community programming at this downtown art-space stop, then pair it with a walk along Georgia Street.
cards.short_summary: A named community art space in Vallejo’s downtown arts district.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Vallejo identifies Artiszen as a downtown community space encouraging artistic growth and lists Artiszen Gallery on Georgia Street.
cards.access_notes: Programming and public access can vary by event; check the venue before visiting.

cards.title: Capitol Stairs Mosaic
cards.subtitle: Capitol Street and Sonoma Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Use the mosaicked stairway as a walking link between the Heritage District and historic downtown; allow time for the steep climb.
cards.short_summary: A documented mosaic stair connection between two historic Vallejo areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Vallejo places the Capitol Stairs Mosaic at the cul-de-sac at 602 Capitol Street and Sonoma Boulevard, connecting the Heritage District to historic downtown.
cards.access_notes: The Heritage District includes steep hills; use care on the stairs.

cards.title: Mare Island Artifact Museum
cards.subtitle: Railroad Avenue and 8th Street corridor
cards.notes: Find Building 46 by the patrol boat with shark’s teeth, then explore artifacts near Alden Park and the historic waterfront.
cards.short_summary: A small museum in a former 1855 pipe shop on Mare Island.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mare Island Historic Park Foundation states that its Artifact Museum is in Building 46 at 1100 Railroad Avenue and 8th Street, across from Alden Park.
cards.source_title: Mare Island Historic Park Foundation Artifact Museum
cards.access_notes: The foundation lists limited weekday and selected-weekend public hours; verify before travel.

cards.title: St. Peter’s Chapel
cards.subtitle: Nimitz Avenue historic-core corridor
cards.notes: Include the chapel on a historic-core walk and look for the Tiffany stained-glass windows referenced by the park foundation’s tour information.
cards.short_summary: A preserved Mare Island chapel included in the historic park’s documented tours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mare Island Historic Park Foundation lists St. Peter’s Chapel and its Tiffany stained-glass windows among sites on its historic Mare Island tours.
cards.source_title: Mare Island Historic Park Foundation Tours
cards.access_notes: Interior access is tour-dependent; contact the foundation for current tour arrangements.

cards.title: USS Vallejo Submarine Sail Memorial
cards.subtitle: Nimitz Avenue historic-core corridor
cards.notes: Make this a short outdoor history stop while walking the historic core; pair it with nearby landmark interpretation rather than entering restricted areas.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor memorial maintained by the Mare Island Historic Park Foundation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mare Island Historic Park Foundation says it oversaw restoration and installation of the USS Vallejo Submarine Sail Memorial in Mare Island’s historic core in 2019.
cards.source_title: About the Mare Island Historic Park Foundation
cards.access_notes: Remain on publicly accessible routes and follow posted site guidance.

cards.title: Mare Island Preserve
cards.subtitle: Mare Island shoreline corridor
cards.notes: Choose a daylight walk through this former naval-ammunition-depot landscape and use the posted entry guidance, limits, and trail conditions before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A city-owned public open-space preserve at Mare Island’s southern end.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Vallejo describes Mare Island Preserve as public park land, approximately 124 acres, and states that it is open daily from 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.
cards.access_notes: City page lists daily access from 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., with visitor and vehicle limits; confirm conditions before visiting.
